title: Erdős #977: Greatest Prime Factor of 2^n - 1
description: Does P(2^n - 1)/n → ∞? Solved by Stewart (2013): P(2^n - 1) ≥ n^{1 + 1/(104 log log n)}. Schinzel (1962) proved P(2^n - 1) > 2n for n > 12.

meta.author: Paul Erdős, Andrzej Schinzel, Cameron Stewart

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős posed this problem around 1965, asking whether the greatest prime factor of $2^n - 1$ grows faster than linearly. The first major progress came from Andrzej Schinzel in 1962, who proved $P(2^n - 1) > 2n$ for all $n > 12$ using algebraic factorization properties of cyclotomic polynomials. Cameron Stewart made further conditional progress in 1974, and finally settled the problem unconditionally in 2013 with the quantitative bound $P(2^n - 1) \ge n^{1 + 1/(104 \log\log n)}$. Stewart's proof combines deep techniques from transcendental number theory (Baker's theory of linear forms in logarithms) with the arithmetic of cyclotomic fields.

The problem sits in a rich tradition connecting prime factorization to exponential sequences. Zsygmondy's theorem (1892) guarantees that $2^n - 1$ has a *primitive* prime factor for $n > 6$ — a prime not dividing $2^k - 1$ for any $k < n$. Such primes satisfy $p \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, immediately giving $P(2^n - 1) \ge n + 1$, but this falls short of the $n^{1+\varepsilon}$ growth Erdős sought. The connection to Mersenne primes ($2^p - 1$ when prime) adds number-theoretic interest: for the 51 known Mersenne primes, $P(M_p) = M_p = 2^p - 1 \gg 2^p$, far exceeding any polynomial bound. A related open problem asks whether $P(n! + 1)/n \to \infty$, where Lai (2021) proved the partial result $\limsup P(n!+1)/n \ge 1 + 9\log 2 \approx 7.238$.
overview.problemStatement: If $P(m)$ denotes the greatest prime divisor of $m$, is it true that $P(2^n - 1)/n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?
overview.text: Does P(2^n - 1)/n → ∞? Solved by Stewart (2013): P(2^n - 1) ≥ n^{1 + 1/(104 log log n)}. Schinzel (1962) proved P(2^n - 1) > 2n for n > 12.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines the greatest prime factor function $P(n)$, Mersenne numbers $M_n = 2^n - 1$, and states the central question. It axiomatizes Stewart's 2013 theorem (the full answer), Schinzel's 1962 bound, Stewart's quantitative growth rate, specific small cases, the Mersenne prime connection, the related $P(n!+1)$ open problem, Zsygmondy's theorem on primitive prime factors, and the multiplicative order connection $\text{ord}_p(2) \mid n$.
keyInsights: **Stewart's resolution (2013)**: $P(2^n - 1) \ge n^{1 + 1/(104 \log\log n)}$, proving $P(2^n-1)/n \to \infty$. The proof uses Baker's theory of linear forms in logarithms applied to the factorization of $2^n - 1$ via cyclotomic polynomials $\Phi_d(2)$ for $d \mid n$

**Schinzel's linear bound (1962)**: $P(2^n - 1) > 2n$ for $n > 12$, using the fact that primitive prime factors of $\Phi_n(2)$ satisfy $p \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ and bounding the remaining factors algebraically

**Zsygmondy's primitive divisors**: For $n > 6$, $2^n - 1$ has a prime factor $p \nmid 2^k - 1$ for all $k < n$; such $p$ has $\text{ord}_p(2) = n$, so $p \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, giving $P(2^n-1) \ge n+1$ — the starting point for all stronger bounds

**Mersenne prime extremes**: When $M_n = 2^n - 1$ is prime, $P(M_n) = 2^n - 1 \gg 2^n$, exponentially exceeding any polynomial bound — these are the extreme cases where the greatest prime factor is as large as possible

**Open analogue $P(n!+1)$**: The question $P(n!+1)/(n\log n) \to \infty$ remains open despite Lai's 2021 partial result; the factorial structure resists the cyclotomic decomposition that enables Stewart's approach for $2^n - 1$
prerequisites: Prime factorization and greatest prime factor

sections.title: Greatest Prime Factor
sections.summary: Defines $P(n)$ as the greatest prime factor of $n$ (returning 0 for $n \le 1$), and proves basic properties: $P(n) \mid n$ and $P(n)$ is prime for $n \ge 2$.
sections.mathContext: $P(n) = \max\{p \in \mathbb{P} : p \mid n\}$ for $n \geq 2$, with $P(0) = P(1) = 0$. This is the central object: Problem 977 asks about the growth of $P(2^n - 1)/n$.

sections.title: Mersenne Numbers
sections.summary: Defines the Mersenne sequence $M_n = 2^n - 1$ and establishes basic properties including $M_n > 0$ and divisibility relations.
sections.mathContext: $M_n = 2^n - 1$. Key factorization: $2^{ab} - 1 = (2^a - 1)(2^{a(b-1)} + \cdots + 1)$, so $M_a \mid M_{ab}$. If $M_n$ is prime, then $n$ must be prime.

sections.title: Main Question and Stewart's Answer
sections.summary: States the central question $P(2^n - 1)/n \to \infty$ and axiomatizes Stewart's 2013 affirmative answer.
sections.mathContext: Does $P(2^n - 1)/n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$? Equivalently: the largest prime factor of $M_n$ grows super-linearly. SOLVED: Stewart (2013) proved YES.

sections.title: Schinzel's Bound
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Schinzel's 1962 result: $P(2^n - 1) > 2n$ for $n > 12$, the first linear-beating bound.
sections.mathContext: Schinzel (1962): $P(2^n - 1) > 2n$ for all $n > 12$. This was the first result showing $P(M_n)$ grows faster than linearly in $n$, using cyclotomic polynomial factorization.

sections.title: Stewart's Quantitative Bound
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the precise growth rate $P(2^n - 1) \ge n^{1 + 1/(104 \log\log n)}$ from Stewart (2013), giving super-polynomial growth.
sections.mathContext: Stewart (2013): $P(2^n - 1) \geq n^{1 + 1/(104 \log\log n)}$ for large $n$. This is super-polynomial ($\omega(n^{1+\varepsilon})$ for any fixed $\varepsilon$), proved using Baker's method on linear forms in logarithms.

sections.title: Small Cases
sections.summary: Provides explicit computations of $P(2^n - 1)$ for small $n$: $P(M_2) = 3$, $P(M_3) = 7$, etc., verifying the bound for initial cases.
sections.mathContext: $P(M_2) = 3$, $P(M_3) = 7$, $P(M_4) = 5$, $P(M_5) = 31$, $P(M_6) = 7$. The ratio $P(M_n)/n$ already exceeds 1 for all these cases; Schinzel's threshold $n > 12$ ensures it exceeds 2.

sections.title: Mersenne Primes
sections.summary: Defines Mersenne primes and proves that when $M_n$ is prime, $P(M_n) = M_n = 2^n - 1$, the extreme case where the bound is trivially satisfied.
sections.mathContext: When $M_n$ is prime, $P(M_n) = 2^n - 1 \gg n$, trivially satisfying any polynomial bound. The interesting case is composite $M_n$, where prime factors may be much smaller than $M_n$ itself.

sections.title: Related: $P(n! + 1)$
sections.summary: States the open analogue: does $P(n! + 1)/(n \log n) \to \infty$? Axiomatizes Lai's (2021) partial result on the limsup.
sections.mathContext: OPEN: does $P(n! + 1)/(n \log n) \to \infty$? Unlike $2^n - 1$, the sequence $n! + 1$ lacks cyclotomic structure, making Baker-type methods ineffective. Lai (2021) proved $\limsup P(n!+1)/(n \log n) = \infty$.

sections.title: Primitive Prime Factors (Zsygmondy)
sections.summary: Defines primitive prime factors ($p \mid 2^n - 1$ with $p \nmid 2^k - 1$ for $k < n$) and axiomatizes Zsygmondy's theorem: existence for $n > 6$.
sections.mathContext: A prime $p$ is a \emph{primitive} factor of $2^n - 1$ if $p \mid 2^n - 1$ but $p \nmid 2^k - 1$ for $0 < k < n$. Zsygmondy (1892): such $p$ exists for all $n > 6$ (exception: $2^6 - 1 = 63 = 7 \cdot 9$).

sections.title: Multiplicative Order Connection
sections.summary: Defines $\text{ord}_p(2)$ and axiomatizes the connection: $p \mid 2^n - 1 \iff \text{ord}_p(2) \mid n$, linking prime factors to the algebraic structure of $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$.
sections.mathContext: $\text{ord}_p(2) = \min\{k \geq 1 : 2^k \equiv 1 \pmod{p}\}$. Then $p \mid 2^n - 1 \iff \text{ord}_p(2) \mid n$. A primitive factor of $M_n$ has $\text{ord}_p(2) = n$, so $p \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, giving $p \geq n + 1$.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures the complete story of Erdős Problem #977: from the basic definitions of the greatest prime factor function and Mersenne numbers, through Schinzel's linear bound (1962) and Stewart's definitive resolution (2013), to the related open problem on $P(n!+1)$ and the foundational roles of Zsygmondy's theorem and multiplicative orders.
conclusion.implications: Stewart's resolution advances the understanding of how prime factors distribute in exponential sequences. The techniques (Baker's method, cyclotomic decomposition) extend to other sequences $a^n - b^n$, and the problem connects to the Mersenne prime search, algebraic number theory, and the distribution of smooth numbers.
openQuestions: Does $P(n! + 1)/(n \log n) \to \infty$? This analogue of the solved problem resists current techniques because $n!+1$ lacks the cyclotomic factorization of $2^n - 1$.
Can the constant 104 in Stewart's bound $P(2^n-1) \ge n^{1+1/(104\log\log n)}$ be significantly reduced? Is $P(2^n-1) \ge n^{1+c}$ for some absolute constant $c > 0$?
What is the typical size of $P(2^n - 1)$ for generic (non-Mersenne-prime) $n$? Heuristics suggest $P(2^n - 1) \approx 2^{cn}$ for some $c > 0$ on average.
How many prime factors does $2^n - 1$ have? The number of distinct prime factors $\omega(2^n-1)$ grows at least as $\log n / \log\log n$ by the prime counting in cyclotomic factors.
